summary.title: Reimplementing “git clone” in Haskell from the bottom up
summary.one_liner: You learn how git's native transport, pkt-line framing, ref advertisement and packfile negotiation fit together by building a minimal git clone client in Haskell.
takeaways: The git:// protocol: a client connects over TCP (port 9418), sends git-upload-pack with a repo path and host, and reads a ref advertisement.
pkt-line framing: each packet starts with a 4-byte hex length that includes the prefix, and 0000 is a flush packet.
Clone negotiation: the client sends want lines with capabilities (e.g. side-band-64k), a flush, and done, then receives the packfile.
Debugging tools such as GIT_TRACE_PACKET and ngrep help verify the wire-level exchange against a real git daemon.
summary.summary: The author re-implements a minimal git clone in Haskell without using git plumbing or existing git libraries, covering only the git:// transport and full clones. The article walks through the clone stages: parsing the URL, reference discovery and capability exchange, want/have negotiation, receiving the packfile, and building the local repository, index and working directory. It shows how to observe the protocol using git daemon, GIT_TRACE_PACKET, ngrep and ipfw, and includes Haskell code for the pkt-line encoder and a TCP client. The article is explicitly about going wide rather than deep, and the code is presented as condensed pseudo code for readers who do not know Haskell.
